summary: Account is brand new (10 IG, 2 LI, 1 BS followers). Data too thin for reliable patterns; weak signals show reels lose 77% viewers in first 3s, chatbot posts earn 39% of lead_gen per reach, question hooks earn 39% of comparison hooks. Instagram bio violates brand rules: names niches (hotels, cafes, gyms, homestays), region (Himachal), promises 24hr delivery, offers free site check outside website posts.
guidance:
- Fix the hook: first 3 seconds must stop scroll; avoid generic openings.
- Rotate hook styles: try comparison or contrast next (question hooks underperform).
- Vary chatbot angles: don't repeat 'same questions' framing; show varied business types in one line.
- Posts must read as a developer sharing real work, never as an ad; no demo claims, no invented results.
- Only offers: pay after approval, or DM for honest fit advice.

instructions.research: List 5-7 common customer questions shared by varied Indian small businesses (e.g. clinic, salon, coaching centre, shop, D2C brand) that a chatbot could handle.
instructions.analysis: Compare the last 3 chatbot posts' hook styles and engagement vs lead_gen posts; note which hook style (comparison/contrast) aligns with higher per-reach earnings.
instructions.writer: Write a comparison-style post contrasting manual reply workload vs chatbot handling for 2-3 example business types; use soft wording ('can reduce', 'helps'), no demo claims, end with DM for honest advice or pay after approval.
instructions.image: Create a clean silhouette or desk-glow style graphic showing a split scene: business owner overwhelmed by messages vs calm with chatbot; no brand logos, no specific business names.
instructions.video: Not needed for today's chatbot image/carousel post.

manual_tips: Update Instagram bio: remove niches, region, timeframe, and free site check; replace with national, multi-industry description and only allowed offers (pay after approval, DM for advice).
Comment thoughtfully on 5 posts from Indian small business owners in different industries (clinic, salon, coaching, shop, D2C) about handling repeat customer queries.
Reply to any existing DMs/comments with honest advice on whether a chatbot fits their business; mention pay after approval.
